1: /**
2:  * The one mapping between the Studio's message model and assistant-ui's.
3:  *
4:  * Kept in one place and pure, so the thread can be tested without a runtime and
5:  * the runtime can be swapped without touching the transcript. Anything the
6:  * conversion does not understand is dropped rather than rendered as raw JSON:
7:  * an unknown part must never reach the screen as machine text.
8:  */
9: 
10: import type { ThreadMessage, ThreadMessageLike } from "@assistant-ui/react";
11: 
12: import type { ChatAttachment, ChatMessage, ChatPart, StudioError } from "../types";
13: import type { UiNode } from "../ui/protocol";
14: 
15: /** The name our generated-surface parts travel under. */
16: export const SURFACE_PART = "odi-surface";
17: 
18: type LikePart = Exclude<ThreadMessageLike["content"], string>[number];
19: 
20: const TOOL_RESULT: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>> = {
21:   ok: { status: "ok" },
22:   error: { status: "error", isError: true },
23:   declined: { status: "declined" },
24: };
25: 
26: function toPart(part: ChatPart): LikePart | null {
27:   switch (part.kind) {
28:     case "text":
29:       return { type: "text", text: part.text };
30: 
31:     case "reasoning":
32:       return { type: "reasoning", text: part.text };
33: 
34:     case "ui":
35:       return { type: `data-${SURFACE_PART}` as const, id: part.id, data: part.node };
36: 
37:     case "source":
38:       return {
39:         type: "source",
40:         sourceType: "document",
41:         id: part.id,
42:         title: part.title,
43:         mediaType: part.mediaType,
44:         ...(part.filename ? { filename: part.filename } : {}),
45:       };
46: 
47:     case "tool": {
48:       const approval = part.approval;
49:       if (approval) {
50:         // A pending write is a question, not a result: the runtime keeps the
51:         // message in `requires-action` until the user answers.
52:         return {
53:           type: "tool-call",
54:           toolCallId: part.id,
55:           toolName: part.name,
56:           args: {},
57:           argsText: "{}",
58:           approval: { id: approval.id, prompt: approval.prompt },
59:         };
60:       }
61:       return {
62:         type: "tool-call",
63:         toolCallId: part.id,
64:         toolName: part.name,
65:         args: {},
66:         argsText: "{}",
67:         result: { ...(TOOL_RESULT[part.status] ?? {}), preview: part.preview ?? "" },
68:         isError: part.status === "error",
69:       };
70:     }
71: 
72:     default:
73:       return null;
74:   }
75: }
76: 
77: function attachmentParts(attachments: ChatAttachment[]) {
78:   return attachments.map((attachment) => ({
79:     id: attachment.id,
80:     type: attachment.contentType.startsWith("image/") ? ("image" as const) : ("document" as const),
81:     name: attachment.name,
82:     contentType: attachment.contentType,
83:     status: { type: "complete" as const },
84:     content: [
85:       {
86:         type: "file" as const,
87:         data: attachment.id,
88:         mimeType: attachment.contentType,
89:         filename: attachment.name,
90:       },
91:     ],
92:   }));
93: }
94: 
95: /**
96:  * A Studio turn as the runtime renders it.
97:  *
98:  * `content` stays the concatenated prose so history replays byte-identically;
99:  * `parts` is what the thread shows.
100:  */
101: export function toThreadMessageLike(message: ChatMessage): ThreadMessageLike {
102:   if (message.role === "notice") {
103:     return {
104:       id: message.id,
105:       role: "system",
106:       content: [{ type: "text", text: message.content }],
107:     };
108:   }
109: 
110:   const parts = (message.parts ?? []).flatMap((part) => {
111:     const converted = toPart(part);
112:     return converted ? [converted] : [];
113:   });
114: 
115:   const content: readonly LikePart[] =
116:     parts.length > 0
117:       ? parts
118:       : message.content
119:         ? [{ type: "text", text: message.content }]
120:         : [];
121: 
122:   const failed = message.error !== undefined;
123: 
124:   return {
125:     id: message.id,
126:     role: message.role,
127:     content,
128:     ...(message.role === "user" && message.attachments?.length
129:       ? { attachments: attachmentParts(message.attachments) }
130:       : {}),
131:     ...(failed
132:       ? {
133:           status: {
134:             type: "incomplete" as const,
135:             reason: "error" as const,
136:             error: message.error as never,
137:           },
138:         }
139:       : {}),
140:     ...(failed || message.retryText
141:       ? {
142:           metadata: {
143:             custom: {
144:               ...(message.error ? { error: message.error } : {}),
145:               ...(message.retryText ? { retryText: message.retryText } : {}),
146:             },
147:           },
148:         }
149:       : {}),
150:   };
151: }
152: 
153: function readCustom(message: ThreadMessage): Record<string, unknown> {
154:   return (message.metadata?.custom ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
155: }
156: 
157: /**
158:  * The inverse: a runtime message back in the Studio's own model.
159:  *
160:  * The runtime hands a branch switch back as the originals it was given, so this
161:  * is only needed when a message arrives from somewhere else — an import, or a
162:  * future remote thread.
163:  */
164: export function toChatMessage(
165:   message: ThreadMessage,
166:   parentId: string | null = null,
167: ): ChatMessage {
168:   const text = message.content
169:     .filter((part) => part.type === "text")
170:     .map((part) => (part as unknown as { text: string }).text)
171:     .join("");
172: 
173:   const custom = readCustom(message);
174:   const parts: ChatPart[] = [];
175: 
176:   for (const part of message.content) {
177:     switch (part.type) {
178:       case "text":
179:         parts.push({ kind: "text", text: part.text });
180:         break;
181: 
182:       case "reasoning":
183:         parts.push({ kind: "reasoning", text: part.text });
184:         break;
185: 
186:       case "source":
187:         parts.push({
188:           kind: "source",
189:           id: part.id,
190:           title: part.sourceType === "url" ? (part.title ?? part.url) : part.title,
191:           mediaType: part.sourceType === "document" ? part.mediaType : "text/html",
192:           ...(part.sourceType === "document" && part.filename
193:             ? { filename: part.filename }
194:             : {}),
195:         });
196:         break;
197: 
198:       case "tool-call": {
199:         const result = part.result as { status?: string; preview?: string } | undefined;
200:         const approval = part.approval;
201:         const awaiting = approval !== undefined && approval.approved === undefined && !part.result;
202:         parts.push({
203:           kind: "tool",
204:           id: part.toolCallId,
205:           name: part.toolName,
206:           status: awaiting
207:             ? "running"
208:             : part.isError
209:               ? "error"
210:               : result?.status === "declined"
211:                 ? "declined"
212:                 : "ok",
213:           ...(result?.preview ? { preview: result.preview } : {}),
214:           ...(awaiting ? { approval: { id: approval.id, prompt: approval.prompt ?? "" } } : {}),
215:         });
216:         break;
217:       }
218: 
219:       case "data":
220:         if (part.name === SURFACE_PART) {
221:           parts.push({
222:             kind: "ui",
223:             id: part.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`,
224:             node: part.data as UiNode,
225:           });
226:         }
227:         break;
228: 
229:       default:
230:         break;
231:     }
232:   }
233: 
234:   const attachments: ChatAttachment[] | undefined = message.attachments?.length
235:     ? message.attachments.map((attachment) => ({
236:         id: attachment.id,
237:         name: attachment.name,
238:         contentType: attachment.contentType ?? "application/octet-stream",
239:         size: 0,
240:       }))
241:     : undefined;
242: 
243:   const role = message.role === "system" ? "notice" : message.role;
244: 
245:   return {
246:     id: message.id,
247:     parentId,
248:     role,
249:     content: text,
250:     ...(parts.length ? { parts } : {}),
251:     ...(attachments ? { attachments } : {}),
252:     ...(custom.error ? { error: custom.error as StudioError } : {}),
253:     ...(custom.retryText ? { retryText: String(custom.retryText) } : {}),
254:   };
255: }
256: 
257: /** The readable text of one appended message, for the Studio's send path. */
258: export function textOf(message: { content: string | readonly { type: string }[] }): string {
259:   if (typeof message.content === "string") {
260:     return message.content.trim();
261:   }
262:   return message.content
263:     .filter((part) => part.type === "text")
264:     .map((part) => (part as unknown as { text: string }).text)
265:     .join("\n")
266:     .trim();
267: }

1: /**
2:  * Turning a dropped file into something the model can actually read.
3:  *
4:  * The client owns this because only the client has the bytes: the sidecar
5:  * receives extracted text (or a data URL for an image), never a file handle.
6:  * Extraction is bounded so one large attachment cannot crowd out the
7:  * conversation, and it is silent about failure — a file we cannot read is shown
8:  * as a name, not dressed up as content.
9:  */
10: 
11: import type { AttachmentAdapter, CompleteAttachment, PendingAttachment } from "@assistant-ui/react";
12: 
13: import type { ChatAttachment } from "../types";
14: 
15: /** How much of a text file the model sees. */
16: export const MAX_ATTACHMENT_CHARS = 20_000;
17: 
18: /** A single image, bounded so a data URL cannot bloat the request. */
19: export const MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
20: 
21: export const ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT = [
22:   "text/*",
23:   ".md",
24:   ".mdx",
25:   ".json",
26:   ".csv",
27:   ".yaml",
28:   ".yml",
29:   ".log",
30:   "image/png",
31:   "image/jpeg",
32:   "image/webp",
33:   "image/gif",
34: ].join(",");
35: 
36: const TEXT_LIKE = /^(text\/|application\/(json|yaml|x-yaml)$)/;
37: const SUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPES = new Set(
38:   ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT.split(",").filter((type) => type.startsWith("image/")),
39: );
40: 
41: export function isTextLike(name: string, contentType: string): boolean {
42:   if (TEXT_LIKE.test(contentType)) {
43:     return true;
44:   }
45:   return /\.(md|mdx|json|csv|ya?ml|txt|log)$/i.test(name);
46: }
47: 
48: export function isImageLike(contentType: string): boolean {
49:   return contentType.startsWith("image/");
50: }
51: 
52: /**
53:  * Why a dropped or pasted file cannot become an attachment, or null if it can.
54:  *
55:  * The file input already honours `accept`; a drop bypasses it, so the same
56:  * rule is applied here rather than letting an unreadable file become a chip
57:  * that promises content the model will never see.
58:  */
59: export function attachmentRejection(file: File): string | null {
60:   if (isImageLike(file.type)) {
61:     if (!SUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPES.has(file.type)) {
62:       return `${file.name} is not an image the studio can read (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF).`;
63:     }
64:     if (file.size > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) {
65:       return `${file.name} is larger than ${Math.floor(MAX_IMAGE_BYTES / (1024 * 1024))} MB.`;
66:     }
67:     return null;
68:   }
69:   if (isTextLike(file.name, file.type)) {
70:     return null;
71:   }
72:   return `${file.name} is not a text or image file the studio can read.`;
73: }
74: 
75: /** A short size for an attachment chip; empty when there is nothing to say. */
76: export function formatFileSize(bytes: number): string {
77:   if (!bytes || bytes < 0) {
78:     return "";
79:   }
80:   if (bytes < 1024) {
81:     return `${bytes} B`;
82:   }
83:   if (bytes < 1024 * 1024) {
84:     return `${Math.round(bytes / 1024)} KB`;
85:   }
86:   return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`;
87: }
88: 
89: function readAsDataUrl(file: File): Promise<string> {
90:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
91:     const reader = new FileReader();
92:     reader.onload = () => resolve(String(reader.result ?? ""));
93:     reader.onerror = () => reject(reader.error ?? new Error("Could not read the file."));
94:     reader.readAsDataURL(file);
95:   });
96: }
97: 
98: /**
99:  * Prepare one file for a turn. Never throws: an unreadable file becomes a
100:  * name-only attachment so the user can still see what they attached.
101:  */
102: export async function prepareAttachment(file: File): Promise<ChatAttachment> {
103:   const base: ChatAttachment = {
104:     id: crypto.randomUUID(),
105:     name: file.name,
106:     contentType: file.type || "application/octet-stream",
107:     size: file.size,
108:   };
109: 
110:   try {
111:     if (isImageLike(base.contentType) && file.size <= MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) {
112:       return { ...base, dataUrl: await readAsDataUrl(file) };
113:     }
114:     if (isTextLike(file.name, base.contentType)) {
115:       const text = await file.text();
116:       return { ...base, text: text.slice(0, MAX_ATTACHMENT_CHARS) };
117:     }
118:   } catch {
119:     /* a file we cannot read is still an attachment the user chose */
120:   }
121: 
122:   return base;
123: }
124: 
125: /**
126:  * The adapter the runtime uses for `ComposerPrimitive.Attachments`.
127:  *
128:  * Prepared attachments are kept by id so `onNew` can hand the turn the same
129:  * extraction the composer showed.
130:  */
131: export function createAttachmentAdapter(): AttachmentAdapter {
132:   return {
133:     accept: ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT,
134: 
135:     async add({ file }): Promise<PendingAttachment> {
136:       return {
137:         id: crypto.randomUUID(),
138:         type: isImageLike(file.type) ? "image" : file.type ? "document" : "file",
139:         name: file.name,
140:         contentType: file.type || "application/octet-stream",
141:         file,
142:         status: { type: "requires-action", reason: "composer-send" },
143:       };
144:     },
145: 
146:     async remove(): Promise<void> {
147:       // Nothing to release: the file never left the browser.
148:     },
149: 
150:     async send(attachment): Promise<CompleteAttachment> {
151:       const file = attachment.file;
152:       const ready = file
153:         ? await prepareAttachment(file)
154:         : {
155:             id: attachment.id,
156:             name: attachment.name,
157:             contentType: attachment.contentType ?? "application/octet-stream",
158:             size: 0,
159:           };
160:       ATTACHMENTS.set(attachment.id, ready);
161:       return {
162:         ...attachment,
163:         status: { type: "complete" },
164:         content: [
165:           {
166:             type: "file",
167:             data: attachment.id,
168:             mimeType: ready.contentType,
169:             filename: ready.name,
170:           },
171:         ],
172:       };
173:     },
174:   };
175: }
176: 
177: /** Process-wide, because the runtime adapter outlives a render. */
178: const ATTACHMENTS = new Map<string, ChatAttachment>();
179: 
180: /** The extraction for one attachment, for showing what was actually sent. */
181: export function preparedAttachmentById(id: string): ChatAttachment | undefined {
182:   return ATTACHMENTS.get(id);
183: }
184: 
185: /** The extraction for the attachments the runtime handed back on a send. */
186: export function preparedAttachments(
187:   attachments: readonly { id: string }[] | undefined,
188: ): ChatAttachment[] {
189:   if (!attachments?.length) {
190:     return [];
191:   }
192:   return attachments.flatMap((attachment) => {
193:     const ready = ATTACHMENTS.get(attachment.id);
194:     return ready ? [ready] : [];
195:   });
196: }

75: function readStudioError(raw: unknown): StudioError {
76:   if (raw && typeof raw === "object" && "code" in raw) {
77:     const error = raw as Partial<StudioError>;
78:     return {
79:       code: String(error.code ?? "internal"),
80:       message: String(error.message ?? "The assistant could not finish this turn."),
81:       detail: error.detail ?? null,
82:       suggestion: error.suggestion ?? null,
83:       retryable: Boolean(error.retryable),
84:       request_id: error.request_id ?? null,
85:     };
86:   }
87:   return {
88:     code: "internal",
89:     message: "The assistant could not finish this turn.",
90:     retryable: true,
91:   };
92: }

804:    * parented to `assistantParentId`, which is how branches stay linked.

807:     async (
808:       base: ChatMessage[],
809:       userTurn: ChatMessage | null,
810:       assistantParentId: string,

812:       if (streaming) {
813:         return;
814:       }

816:       const history: ChatMessage[] = userTurn ? [...base, userTurn] : base;
817: 
818:       const assistantId = newTurnId();
819:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
820:       setMessages([
821:         ...history,
822:         { role: "assistant", id: assistantId, parentId: assistantParentId, content: "", parts: [] },
823:       ]);
824:       setStreaming(true);
825:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
826:       setOfflineReply(false);
827: 
828:       const controller = new AbortController();
829:       abortRef.current = controller;
830: 
831:       let content = "";
832:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
833:       let steps: RunStep[] = [];
834:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
835:       let terminal = false;
836:       let stopped = false;

838:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
839:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
840:       // above all cards.
841:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
842:         if (!text) {
843:           return;
844:         }
845:         content += text;
846:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
847:         parts =
848:           last?.kind === "text"

853:       // The turn owns its own timeline, so a finished run stays inspectable and
854:       // the next turn starts from nothing without a reset elsewhere.
855:       const publish = () => {
856:         setMessages((prev) => {
857:           if (prev.length <= assistantIndex) {

860:           const next = [...prev];
861:           const retryText = userTurn?.content ?? base[base.length - 1]?.content ?? "";

863:             role: "assistant",
864:             id: assistantId,
865:             parentId: assistantParentId,

883:             }
884:             break;
885:           }
886:           case "delta": {
887:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
888:             publish();
889:             break;
890:           }
891:           case "ui": {
892:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
893:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
894:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());

903:           }

925:           }

930:             }

932:           }

936:               setMemory((prev) =>
937:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)

940:               );

942:             break;
943:           }

946:             break;
947:           case "connector": {

949:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
950:               setMessages((prev) => [

981:             api_key: settings.api_key,
982:             model: settings.model_name,

2:  * The wire contract for agent-composed UI.
3:  *
4:  * A payload is a tree of `{ type, props, children }` nodes validated against a
5:  * catalog manifest. The manifest is plain JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 subset),
6:  * so the same document can be handed to the model as a tool schema and used
7:  * here to validate what comes back. Nothing is eval'd, no HTML is injected, and
8:  * every node is bounded before it can reach React.
9:  *
10:  * Parsing is deliberately forgiving where it is safe (unknown props are
11:  * stripped, unknown component types degrade to a visible fallback) and strict

13:  */

152:   raw: Record<string, unknown>,
153:   schema: UiPropSchema,
154:   depth: number,
155: ): { ok: true; value: Record<string, unknown> } | { ok: false } {
156:   const properties = schema.properties ?? {};
157:   const result: Record<string, unknown> = {};

159:   for (const key of schema.required ?? []) {
160:     if (!(key in raw)) {

162:     }
163:   }
164: 
165:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(raw)) {
166:     const propertySchema = properties[key];
167:     if (!propertySchema) {
168:       // Unknown props are stripped rather than trusted.
169:       continue;
170:     }
171:     const validated = validateValue(value, propertySchema, depth);
172:     if (!validated.ok) {
173:       if ((schema.required ?? []).includes(key)) {
174:         return { ok: false };
175:       }
176:       continue;
177:     }

184: function describePropFailure(entry: UiCatalogEntry, key: string): string {
185:   const schema = entry.props.properties?.[key];
186:   if (!schema) {

188:   }
189:   if (schema.enum) {

191:   }
192:   if (schema.type === "number" || schema.type === "integer") {
193:     const bounds =
194:       schema.minimum !== undefined || schema.maximum !== undefined
195:         ? ` between ${schema.minimum ?? "-∞"} and ${schema.maximum ?? "∞"}`
196:         : "";
197:     return `prop "${key}" must be a ${schema.type}${bounds}`;
198:   }
199:   if (schema.type === "array") {
200:     return `prop "${key}" must be an array of valid items`;
201:   }
202:   if (schema.type === "object") {
203:     return `prop "${key}" must be an object with the documented fields`;
204:   }
205:   if (schema.type === "boolean") {
206:     return `prop "${key}" must be a boolean`;
207:   }
208:   return `prop "${key}" must be a ${schema.type ?? "valid value"}`;
209: }

211: function parseNode(raw: unknown, depth: number, state: ParseState): ParseResult {
212:   if (depth > UI_LIMITS.maxDepth) {
213:     return { ok: false, reason: `UI tree exceeds the maximum depth of ${UI_LIMITS.maxDepth}` };
214:   }
215:   state.nodes += 1;
216:   if (state.nodes > UI_LIMITS.maxNodes) {
217:     return { ok: false, reason: `UI tree exceeds the maximum of ${UI_LIMITS.maxNodes} nodes` };
218:   }

220:   if (!isPlainObject(raw)) {

222:   }

231:   }
232:   if (raw.children !== undefined && !Array.isArray(raw.children)) {

234:   }
